about.en: Against a turtled partner: one hand feeds deep across the neck to take the far lapel, and the turnover and the single-hand strangle arrive together, so defending one exposes the other. Strangles are senior material and always released on the tap.

en: Feed the lapel hand deep before you start the roll
The turnover and the strangle are one movement, not two
Apply gradually: the tap comes fast from a turtled partner
Your partner is on hands and knees, defending, and you are at their right side.
Reach your right hand over their neck and feed it under their throat to grip their far lapel, thumb inside.
Take their near arm or belt with your left hand and drag them towards you, rolling them over their right shoulder.
As they land on their side or back, your gripping forearm is already across the throat: Kata-te-jime is on.
Squeeze gradually by drawing the lapel and pressing the forearm; release completely the instant they tap.

receiving.en: A hand snakes under your throat while you are turtled, and the roll that follows lands you with a forearm already across your neck. Defend the lapel hand before the roll starts by tucking your chin and gripping their sleeve; once the strangle closes, tap at once rather than testing it.

viNotes.en: Their turtle is found by hand: the line of the spine, the neck, the far lapel under the throat. Feed the hand by feel along the collar rather than reaching for where the lapel looks to be, and let the roll come from the belt or the arm in your other hand. The forearm across the throat tells you the strangle is placed. Tighten slowly and release on the tap, which you will feel through the arm before you would ever see it.
